index.summary: Close the active-iteration requirement and task change workflow with high-level atomic helpers and enforced replanning invariants.

task.title: Close the active-iteration change and replanning workflow
task.objective: Implement a complete, agent-usable workflow for technical elaboration, task addition/revision/splitting, requirement proposal/replacement planning, material-change capture, replanning freezes, atomic task graph reconciliation, and owner-gated continuation without direct managed XML editing.
task.rationale: The current v1 authority model is sound, but active-iteration changes still require low-level transaction composition and rely on Skill-only rules for frozen execution and immutable completed work.

constraints.constraint: No high-level helper may approve, supersede, withdraw, accept, reject, waive, or complete product state without iteration confirm and current-interaction owner instruction.
Approved requirements and completed tasks remain immutable historical objects; corrections use successor objects and explicit provenance.
Each technical business action either commits its full spec/tasks effect with revision checks or leaves both documents unchanged.
Existing public v1 commands and valid workspaces remain compatible.

acceptance.criterion: Public schema-aware helpers cover task add, task revise, task split, requirement propose, material change propose, and replanning change apply without callers composing low-level XPath transactions.
When an iteration is replanning, Core rejects technical execution progress while allowing explicit planning reconciliation and terminal dispositions needed to form the new plan.
Core rejects low-level or high-level metadata/content rewrites of done, transferred, superseded, and cancelled tasks, while still allowing append-only historical records where explicitly permitted.
Requirement replacement preserves the old approved requirement, adds a proposed successor with provenance, requires owner dispositions, and validates task impact mapping before continuation.

Material change propose/apply actions use expected spec/tasks revisions, deterministic output, durable idempotency, whole-workspace prospective validation, one writer lock, and recovery-backed multi-document commits.

A public-CLI end-to-end scenario proves active implementation, unexpected finding, frozen replanning, requirement replacement, task split/reconciliation, owner continuation, resumed execution, and unchanged state for negative cases.
Skill, templates, CLI help, README, and normative docs teach the exact change decision tree, authority stops, XPath resume behavior, and retry semantics.

context.summary: Build the missing high-level change control layer on top of existing XML authority guards, revisioned transactions, task state machine, and owner confirmation engine.

key_points.point: Separate technical change preparation/application from owner replan/continue confirmation.
Do not introduce a global current-task pointer; resumed work remains XPath-derived from task states.
Use successor requirements/tasks and provenance instead of rewriting decided or terminal historical objects.

record.summary: Started high-level active-iteration change workflow closure after a clean 541-test baseline.

Verified the active-iteration change workflow after independent audit and corrective closure: build.cmd passed 411 Core and 148 CLI tests with zero warnings or errors; the focused public-CLI material-change lifecycle passed; all request templates validate; git diff check and whole-workspace schema and semantic validation passed.

Completed the technical change-workflow closure. Active iterations now support bounded task elaboration, owner-gated requirement replacement, frozen material-change replanning, atomic reconciliation, durable retry receipts, and XPath-derived resumption without rewriting decided product state.

index.summary: Add a low-friction Quick Task entry point while preserving the normal Task model, traceability, and authority boundaries.

task.title: Add the Quick Task workflow
task.objective: Implement task quick as a compact CLI helper for bounded ad hoc work, including operational iteration origins, optional atomic create-and-start, dry-run preview, deterministic metadata, and normal XPath resumption.
task.rationale: The formal task.add XML flow is unnecessarily expensive for medium-sized temporary technical work, but bypassing Task state, acceptance, history, and owner authority would create untracked execution.

constraints.constraint: Quick is an input convenience only; persisted work remains a normal Task in the iteration tasks.xml document and uses the existing lifecycle.
Operational Quick Tasks cannot satisfy product Requirement coverage or modify owner-controlled product state.
The start option must publish create-and-start as one tasks.xml revision with complete generated history, never as a hidden partially successful two-command sequence.
Existing task add/update/split/revise commands, schemas, workspaces, and two-phase XPath selection remain compatible.

acceptance.criterion: The public task quick command accepts compact title, scope, done-when, why, origin, dependency, index-term, iteration, revision, start, and dry-run inputs; it auto-discovers the unique active iteration when omitted and fails explicitly on ambiguity.

A Quick Task either implements explicitly selected existing requirements or, when no requirement is supplied, has exactly one current-iteration supports origin; mixed or external iteration origins are rejected.

Iteration-origin operational Tasks can execute in an active iteration and block technical iteration readiness while non-terminal, but never count as Requirement implementation coverage or product acceptance.

Without start the command atomically creates one pending Task; with start it atomically creates one in-progress Task with created_at, updated_at, started_at, start history, and one revision increment.

Quick Task writes enforce writer locking, exact or safely auto-resolved revision preconditions, monotonic UTC timestamps, document and request limits, prospective validation, durable idempotency receipts, and deterministic machine output.
Dry-run returns the complete generated Task/request representation without modifying any managed document, revision, or temporary transaction state.
Skill, README, CLI contract, help, templates or examples, and public-CLI end-to-end tests teach when to use revise, quick, change propose, or backlog and prove XPath resume behavior.

context.summary: Implemented and independently reviewed the normal-Task Quick entry path, atomic start, operational origin, shared dry-run preflight, and low-level transition guards.

key_points.point: Use Quick Task only for bounded work intended to execute now; deferred work belongs in backlog.
If execution crosses product, architecture, policy, or acceptance boundaries, stop and use change propose rather than rewriting the Quick Task.
Started Quick Tasks are discovered by the existing in-progress XPath query; no global current-task pointer is introduced.

Task addition receipt.
